answer: Web-of-trust vouching resists sybils: an identity gains weight only when established peers stake their own standing to vouch for it, and those vouches must come from distinct, unrelated accounts. A fake bolted onto the basalt edge has no genuine sponsors, so it stays an isolated reef with no inbound trust. A swarm can vouch for itself endlessly, but the counting rule discounts inward-only loops, leaving the clones on a bare ledge with zero real weight.
